Jones Framework

Derivation of the calibrated sample Jones matrix

For an ideal linear polarizer at angle θ\thetaθ, define the Jones vector

e(θ)=(cos⁡θsin⁡θ).\mathbf e(\theta)= \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta \\ \sin\theta \end{pmatrix}.e(θ)=(cosθsinθ​).

For a measured 2×22\times22×2 transfer matrix

T=(t00t01t10t11),\mathbf T= \begin{pmatrix} t_{00} & t_{01} \\ t_{10} & t_{11} \end{pmatrix},T=(t00​t10​​t01​t11​​),

the complex field measured with the analyzer at α\alphaα and the input polarizer at β\betaβ is

mα,β=eT(α) T e(β).m_{\alpha,\beta} = \mathbf e^{\mathsf T}(\alpha)\, \mathbf T\, \mathbf e(\beta).mα,β​=eT(α)Te(β).

The four measured configurations yield

M0=m0∘,0∘=t00,M90=m90∘,90∘=t11,M45,0=m45∘,0∘=t00+t102,M45,90=m45∘,90∘=t01+t112.\begin{aligned} M_0 &=m_{0^\circ,0^\circ}=t_{00},\\ M_{90} &=m_{90^\circ,90^\circ}=t_{11},\\ M_{45,0} &=m_{45^\circ,0^\circ} =\frac{t_{00}+t_{10}}{\sqrt 2},\\ M_{45,90} &=m_{45^\circ,90^\circ} =\frac{t_{01}+t_{11}}{\sqrt 2}. \end{aligned}M0​M90​M45,0​M45,90​​=m0∘,0∘​=t00​,=m90∘,90∘​=t11​,=m45∘,0∘​=2​t00​+t10​​,=m45∘,90∘​=2​t01​+t11​​.​

Therefore, the two unmeasured matrix elements are

t10=2 M45,0−M0,t01=2 M45,90−M90.t_{10}=\sqrt 2\,M_{45,0}-M_0, \qquad t_{01}=\sqrt 2\,M_{45,90}-M_{90}.t10​=2​M45,0​−M0​,t01​=2​M45,90​−M90​.

The complete transfer matrix measured with the sample installed is therefore

Tsam=(M02 M45,90−M902 M45,0−M0M90).\mathbf T_{\mathrm{sam}}= \begin{pmatrix} M_0 & \sqrt 2\,M_{45,90}-M_{90}\\ \sqrt 2\,M_{45,0}-M_0 & M_{90} \end{pmatrix}.Tsam​=(M0​2​M45,0​−M0​​2​M45,90​−M90​M90​​).

The reference measurements give the analogous matrix

Tref=(R02 R45,90−R902 R45,0−R0R90).\mathbf T_{\mathrm{ref}}= \begin{pmatrix} R_0 & \sqrt 2\,R_{45,90}-R_{90}\\ \sqrt 2\,R_{45,0}-R_0 & R_{90} \end{pmatrix}.Tref​=(R0​2​R45,0​−R0​​2​R45,90​−R90​R90​​).

In the convention used here, the reference (system) response acts on the left of the sample Jones matrix:

Tsam=Tref Jsam.\mathbf T_{\mathrm{sam}} = \mathbf T_{\mathrm{ref}}\, \mathbf J_{\mathrm{sam}}.Tsam​=Tref​Jsam​.

Provided that

det⁡ ⁣(Tref)≠0,\det\!\left(\mathbf T_{\mathrm{ref}}\right)\neq0,det(Tref​)=0,

solving the matrix equation from the left yields

Jsam=Tref−1Tsam.\boxed{ \mathbf J_{\mathrm{sam}} = \mathbf T_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1} \mathbf T_{\mathrm{sam}} }.Jsam​=Tref−1​Tsam​​.

Numerically, the notebook evaluates this as

LinearSolve[Treference, Tsample]\boxed{ \texttt{LinearSolve[Treference, Tsample]} }LinearSolve[Treference, Tsample]​

rather than explicitly forming the inverse. This is both clearer and numerically more stable. The order is essential because Jones matrices generally do not commute:

Tref−1Tsam≠TsamTref−1.\mathbf T_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}\mathbf T_{\mathrm{sam}} \neq \mathbf T_{\mathrm{sam}}\mathbf T_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}.Tref−1​Tsam​=Tsam​Tref−1​.

Let's load the Jones matrix component:

PacletDirectoryLoad[NotebookDirectory[]]; <<JerryI`THzTDSTools`; <<JerryI`THzTDSTools`Jones`;

Linear Birefringence

Orienting an unknown tetragonal sample with strong linear birefringence

Load the test data measured in four different polarizer–analyzer configurations:

testData = NotebookRead[NotebookStore["bootes-1e7"]]; {listSam, listRef} = testData; listSam // Shallow listRef // Shallow {{Times[1/4, Pi], 0} -> QuantityArray[...], {Times[1/2, Pi], Times[1/2, Pi]} -> QuantityArray[...], {Times[1/4, Pi], Times[1/2, Pi]} -> QuantityArray[...], {0, 0} -> QuantityArray[...]} {{Times[1/4, Pi], 0} -> QuantityArray[...], {Times[1/4, Pi], Times[1/2, Pi]} -> QuantityArray[...], {Times[1/2, Pi], Times[1/2, Pi]} -> QuantityArray[...], {0, 0} -> QuantityArray[...]}

Now, d contains a series of Jones matrices—one for each measured frequency—rather than a single matrix. We can extract the matrix at a specific frequency:

d[Quantity[1.25, "Terahertz"]] // MatrixForm (*GB[*){{0.5963015865631917` -0.05208772491777156` I(*|*),(*|*)0.09143847094395247` -0.03082360560322146` I}(*||*),(*||*){-0.06687365647459285`+0.09671165603605036` I(*|*),(*|*)-0.203333895979706`-0.7882630234360012` I}}(*||*)(*1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAo5gUSYZmp5S6pyflFiSX5RcFsQBHfxJKizAoAs04KOA==*)(*]GB*)

In this particular case, the sample was mounted at a small angle relative to the laboratory coordinate system. Because the mirrors rotate the polarization, the eigenvectors also exhibit slight ellipticity. We can inspect these vectors directly:

OpticalAxisAnalysis[d[Quantity[1.25, "Terahertz"]]]; %[["Eigenpolarizations", All, {"JonesVector", "AzimuthDeg"}]] // TableView (*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["F19f09a28-0a21-4427-9484-a20231c0437c"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgUJG1qmGVgmGlnoGiQaGeqamBiZ61qaWJjoJhoZGBkbJhuYGJsnAwCFpRS5"*)(*]VB*)

We can also average the Jones matrix over a frequency interval, which may provide a better estimate:

OpticalAxisAnalysis[d, Quantity[Interval[{1.15, 1.5}], "Terahertz"]]; %[["Eigenpolarizations", All, {"JonesVector", "AzimuthDeg"}]] // TableView (*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["F6998f186-9499-42a3-8a93-a2277308d6ce"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgUJm1laWqQZWpjpWppYWuqaGCUa61okWhrrJhoZmZsbG1ikmCWnAgCF/xUd"*)(*]VB*)

Extracting Material Parameters

Assuming that the ellipticity is caused by optical misalignment, we can neglect it and use linearized eigenvectors:

basis = OpticalAxisAnalysis[d, Quantity[Interval[{1.15, 1.5}], "Terahertz"]]["LinearizedEigenvectors"] {{0.9997855134235536`,0.020710556448375564`},{-0.040682908928530645`,0.9991721077577741`}}

When expressed in basis, our 2×22\times 22×2 transmission matrix becomes nearly diagonal. Repeating this process at every frequency allows us to extract the sample transmission for each optical eigenmode:

t1122 = OpticalAxesTransmission[d, basis]; FrequencySpectrumTrim /@ %; ListLinePlot[%[[All, All, {1, 2}]], PlotRange -> {{0.25, 1.55}, {0, 1}}, Frame -> True, FrameLabel -> {"\[Omega] (THz)", "t(\[Omega])"}, PlotLegends -> {"Polarization 1", "Polarization 2"} ] (*VB[*)(Legended[ToExpression[FrontEndRef["Fbf1786b5-d46a-4e36-9fd8-c722891df115"], InputForm], Placed[LineLegend[{Directive[PointSize[0.006944444444444445], RGBColor[0.24, 0.6, 0.8], AbsoluteThickness[2]], Directive[PointSize[0.006944444444444445], RGBColor[0.95, 0.627, 0.1425], AbsoluteThickness[2]]}, {"Pol 1", "Pol 2"}, LegendMarkers -> {{False, Automatic}, {False, Automatic}}, Joined -> {True, True}, LabelStyle -> {}, LegendLayout -> "Column"], After, Identity]])(*,*)(*"1:eJylUk0vQ0EUre+PkGCNsLDs4hXVLpqXooS0UZ7Yz3tzh4npDPPmoWLrR7C18wu6tunOwsYPYCMSiX9gPqLShoi4i5N5992559xzZzYUO6QnlUrFoxr2KJyuQiQkUkIGAzpThn3gOONKhjWUMNX/TCHpMrkJDWtScFXiuHQGUaJQyCCYM+mQeEu5bLiYxgtZlF6A+Ww6T3AuHS1lMrm8h4nnLZJu06VXw06i7w2aAyC8xVndZndlAh01RkYADCJLFfcZKsRicCL7NVQZigCT/k/RZcrBTfLVqkxj5W4MaVilUvejJ+CmMqmqoFwF9BzkVPN4snl84btyK3F9eUUwIWVj+vJ1u3Hvy3kbT768vjLx4rtG4xqKYSxYomD3gEaHHOKYGhH/5yY23nx5+/5QCceefVkYfrw5Ktz9zt3mQtBnGdmM1zpl2i23j8MZWEHyEGTc4WPb19dG7CzFRIkaUjT6a5VlNjvc1G5Ax+paj+OHV+L2jkJggaozIKnv9drSkdZ0ZVQXiQoMqfY4qXGrskiUHtl4v4GBK6rqH9Ox0No="*)(*]VB*)
